note: Every marriage in this archive that a document places, in order. A marriage is where two lines join, and it is also the moment a family chooses a town, a church and a witness — so the column that matters most here is not the date but the place.

rows.n: He was about seventeen. She died before March 1825, and at least one child came after that — so there was a second marriage nobody had recorded until 2026.
She was a widow; his origin is left blank on a page where the clerk filled everyone else's in. The blank predates the 1840 death notice by twenty-three years.
Both were sixteen. The Nautilus passenger roll the following year makes them twenty — a second age overstatement in the same twelve months.
A second van der Merwe, named only on her son's 1908 death notice. No place and no date: the marriage is known because a child of it was born about June 1828.
Eight months before her sister married in the same town.
THE JUNCTION. Booysen meets Mountjoy, and the two surnames that carry this archive are joined. He signed her death notice twenty-five years later.
Certificate 735. Thirteen children — and their forenames run out through three more surnames.

**THIS ROW SAID 1850 UNTIL 28 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND THEIR ELDEST SON WAS BORN IN 1847.** The 1850 came from the word **“probably”**, written by their son R. P. Barry on his father's death notice in 1915 — the same son who had written **“Unknown”** on his mother's notice three months earlier. **The archive's own kin file drew JOHN AUGUSTUS BARRY II, born 13 March 1847, under that marriage the whole time.** A gate refuses that arrangement now. **THE DATE AND PLACE ARE FROM A BOOK AND ARE MARKED `inf` ACCORDINGLY:** *Prof. C. Pama's South African family genealogies*, reported to David by a correspondent in **November 1999** — *“John who married Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Kolbe in Colesberg on feb 23, 1846”*. **What makes it safe to adopt is not the book.** It is that this archive's own people file has said *married 1846* all along, and that 1850 is arithmetically impossible. **The Colesberg marriage register would make it `doc`**, and it has not been read. An Irish carpenter and a Settler's daughter. Both their death notices survive, filed on the same day in 1915, and the two disagree about when he died. **AND THIS ARCHIVE INDEPENDENTLY PUTS THE FAMILY AT COLESBERG THAT FORTNIGHT.** Her brother the Commandant had a son, **GEORGE AUGUSTUS, baptised at Colesberg on 8 MARCH 1846** — **thirteen days after this wedding**, in the same town, at the same font. Their father the Settler's own death notice had been signed at Colesberg in January 1845. **Pama's date is not corroborated by Pama**: it is corroborated by a baptism register this archive read on its own account, for a different household, a fortnight later.
The second marriage his own death notice refuses to name. A christening named her in the end — the oldest open question on this site, answered by a baptism rather than a death.

**THE IMAGE IS READ, AND THE REGISTER SAYS THE WORD IN ITS OWN HAND.** She is entered **“ANNA JACOBA KOLBE, GEB: VAN DER MERWE”**, aged **46**, condition **WEDUWE**, no occupation, living at **LEEUWBERG (BLOEMF.)** — the farm her first husband died on. He is **FRANCIS McCABE**, **53**, condition **WEDUWNAAR**, **LANDDROST**, of Bloemfontein. So this archive's duplicate is withdrawn on the document and not merely on the arithmetic: she is the Commandant's widow, under his surname, as the tree's “about April 1871” never quite said. Married by **LICENTIE** rather than banns, with the consent column empty because both were of age; entry **874**, stamped 5167; solemnised by **GUSTAV RADLOFF, V.D.M.** in the church of the Nederduitsch Gereformeerde Gemeente at Bloemfontein. **SHE SIGNED IT HERSELF**, *A. Jacoba Kolbe geboren van der merwe*, which is the first time this archive has seen her hand. Witnesses: an illegible first signature and **[J or F]. M. DE VILLIERS**. FamilySearch 1:1:6ZH1-PJDY, image 3:1:3Q9M-CSK8-G98P-6, DGS 008145483 image 186 of 283.

**THE IMAGE IS READ, AND IT NAMES NO FATHERS — THIS FORM HAS NO COLUMN FOR THEM.** He is **23** and a **VEEBOER**; she is **17** with no occupation; both are entered once, across the two lines, as **JONGELIEDEN**. **AND THEY LIVE ON THE SAME FARM.** His residence is **LEEUWBERG (BLFN.)** and hers is **“DITO”** — the farm the Commandant died on, where the register had placed his widow eleven months earlier. Married on **GEBODEN**, the banns, with consent given by the **MOEDER**: the bride was a minor and her father had been dead fifteen weeks. Entry stamped **5202**; solemnised by **GUSTAV RADLOFF, V.D.M.** at Bloemfontein. Both signed — *J. H. Kolbe* and *Rose Maria Mc Cabe*. **THE SECOND WITNESS IS A KOLBE**: the signature reads **G. A. KOLBE**, and the first is the same illegible hand that witnessed the 1871 marriage. FamilySearch 1:1:6ZHB-XQ1R, image 3:1:3Q9M-CSK8-G98V-M, DGS 008145483 image 221 of 283.
He signs as a BOER. The signature on this register is the one this archive has spent most of its time arguing about: is the letter a z or an s?
Twenty-two and twenty. Five of their eight children are named for a parent or a grandparent, and one dead daughter's name was given again four years later.
In community of property. Their two death notices were typed on the same afternoon in February 1938, hers three and a half years late — “death not reported”.
In community of property. She died in 1930 and he did not report it until 1943.
“In woonhuis D. Schoeman” — in the house of a man tried as a Cape Rebel the month before, under martial law, witnessed by him.
Certificate 13. He is 22 and a MIJNWERKER of Dugmore Mijn; she is 16 and her parents had to consent. Their son had been born four months earlier.
The same village where her father had died in 1905. His 1942 notice enters her as “born Booyzen”, with a z, from her own dictation.
A tree nurseryman and a girl of eighteen who were first cousins once removed — the Barry line closing on itself sixty-five years after it left.
Where this archive stops and the Lerena one begins.
